title: Electrochemically Facilitated Transport of CO2 between Gas Diffusion Electrodes in Flat and Hollow Fiber Geometries

compounds.name: NQ-G2
compounds.quote: 2,3-di(2-methoxyethoxy)-1,4-naphthoquinone, the LQ with a shorter glyme tail.38 This molecule is a solid at room temperature, but we found that the ether functionality still imparted excellent solubility in ionic liquids. With [emim][tcm] we observed no solubility limit at ambient temperature; instead, the solid readily formed a liquid with the addition of even small amounts of ionic liquid. We thus chose to investigate the performance of this quinone, termed NQ-G2 for the remainder of this work, in [emim][tcm].

measurements.quote: In DMSO under N2, NQ-G2 exhibits two redox waves at −1.2 and −1.8 V vs Fc/Fc+, corresponding to reduction to a semiquinone radical anion species and then the dianion quinone.

observations.quote: It was demonstrated that in this ionic liquid, the quinone redox behavior was similar to that of other nonaqueous systems, forming dianion adduct species with CO2 in their reduced state.

raw.quote: 92.7% of the theoretical capacity was achieved, demonstrating that the quinone does react with 2 CO2 per molecule, that a 1e−/CO2 process should be expected, and that NQ-G2 is able to capture CO2 from a dilute feed stream in the ionic liquid system.
